title: Rapid patch and communication lane for mixed-topology canary anomalies
creator: Aisha Mehta
description: During a staggered model rollout we observed intermittent quality regressions and latency spikes confined to slices that traversed heterogeneous routing between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private planes. This ticket coordinates a fast, minimally-invasive runtime patch, a KV-cache reconciliation step, and a defined customer/internal communication lane so affected tenants see a predictable fallback while we validate a full corrective rollout.
runbook_steps: 1. Triage: Confirm tenant slices showing regression via per-tenant quality dashboard and logs (Grafana link in field 'dashboards').
2. Isolate: Temporarily divert affected traffic to fallback model variant (route config change, run in 'staged-fallback' lane for 10 minutes).
3. Patch: Apply runtime hotpatch (opt kernel selection + guard for int8 quantized path) to Dedicated pool nodes in one AZ, then to Private control plane nodes. See PRs in 'linked_prs'.
4. KV reconciliation: Execute targeted KV cache invalidation for tenant slice keys, then warm prefix cache with golden prompts for 30 minutes.
5. Validate: Run the golden prompt suite (50 prompt set) against pinned variant and patched runtime; require >=95% pass rate before broad rollout.
6. Rollforward: If validation passes, expand patch to remaining nodes using staggered 3-stage rollout with automatic abort on SLO breach (>3 customer errors/min or latency p95 > 2x baseline).
7. Rollback: If validation fails, revert routing to prior stable variant and rollback hotpatch with coordinated KV reconciliation to match state.
8. Communicate: Send customer-facing and internal updates at each stage using templates in 'communication_plan'.
9. Post-incident: Run RCA, update model onboarding checklist to include kernel-selection validation for mixed-topology rollouts.
rollback_playbook: If customers continue to see regressions after staged patching: 1) Immediately flip route to last-known-good variant for affected slices; 2) Trigger automated rollback job that first quiesces acceptors, then reverts runtime package and clears ephemeral caches; 3) Open an incident bridge (zoom) and assign tenant liaison; 4) Escalate to on-call runtime engineer and the person who merged the hotpatch; 5) Publish rollback confirmation and affected tenant list to #incidents and external status page.
communication_plan: Internal: Create dedicated triage channel (#incident-eng-eng-582920) and invite PM, SRE, runtime leads, and solutions engineer. Provide hourly status with template: current mitigation, verification results, next step, ETA.

Customer: Draft customer-safe message: we detected anomalous output quality for a small subset of customers during a rollout; we have routed you to a verified fallback and are deploying a targeted patch; expected restoration within 2 hours. Provide link to status page and contact for high-touch customers.
Executive: One-line impact summary for leadership: affected 0.8% of active tenants, latency increase spike to p95 observed for mixed-topology traffic; P0 remediation in flight.
